comments.author: @Nicholas_Buck
comments.text: Between 1990 and 2020 my friend and I frequently enjoyed the excellent (catch and release) fly fishing on the Cheslatta River between the Holy Cross Forestry Road and the second Cheslatta Falls, as well as the large pool at the base of the Falls. The fishing varied significantly depending on the volume of water released from the Skins Lake Spillway. Usually, the flow was quite low (around 1200 cubic feet per second) which allowed us easy access to the river and the pools holding many large rainbows. After July 18th, Alcan was required to increase the flow (to up to 12,000 cfs) to cool down the Nechako River to allow the Stuart Lake run of sockeyes to reach their spawning grounds around Stuart Lake. This regime was only partially successful because the water released at Skins Lake was warm water from the surface, and the increased flow was a burden on the salmon already exhausted from swimming up the Fraser River to its confluence with the Nechako. The fishing was still good with the greater flow, but the river was quite dangerous; falling in would probably have been fatal. The roughly 10 km stretch of (mostly) dry canyon from the Falls up to the Kenney Dam is now a conservation area.

replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: Thanks for sharing this, Nicholas. Thirty years of fishing there gives you a perspective that maps and reports can’t. Your description of how the releases changed access to the pools, and how dangerous the river became, really brings that home.
